newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shareholder sues Sumitomo over meeting.
newsitem.headline: Shareholder sues Sumitomo over meeting.

text.p: An individual shareholder of trading house Sumitomo Corp filed a lawsuit against it calling for repeal of resolutions passed at its June shareholders' meeting, an Osaka District Court spokesman said on Thursday.
The meeting was held only two weeks after Sumitomo announced it had amassed an estimated $1.8 billion loss from unauthorised copper trades over a 10-year period.

"I thought it was strange that the shareholders' meeting ended without any objections, despite the occurrence of such a major incident," Kazuyoshi Yuoka, who filed the suit, told Japanese public television station NHK.
Sumitomo Corp said in a statement it had not been notified of the suit and therefore could not comment on it.

"If this case is requesting the repeal of resolutions at our general shareholders' meeting, it is our belief that the meeting was held for the shareholders themselves and that procedurally it was in accord with commercial law, and therefore there are no problems with it," the statement said.

According to Japanese media reports, Yuoka, who holds 2,000 shares in Sumitomo, filed suit calling for the repeal of four resolutions passed at the shareholders' meeting after he was allegedly denied an opportunity to ask questions of Sumitomo executives.
Yuoka could not immediately be reached for comment.

Sumitomo jumped back into the headlines last week when, after months of official silence on the copper scandal, it announced that it raised its estimated copper trading losses to $2.6 billion from $1.8 billion.
